title: Retry-safe VCF Automation lease-policy convergence against a reference-derived contract
prompt:
`vcfa-policy-sync` is the small Python package our platform CI runs to keep VCF Automation deployment-lease policies in step with what is checked into git. It targets VCF Automation in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 -- the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation.

VCF Automation publishes no machine-readable API specification, so `docs/contract.json` is a hand transcription of the Broadcom xAPIs reference pages recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. Read the contract first. It is the authority for paths, methods, headers, body fields and retry behaviour, and it marks which parts are literal transcription and which are inference.

`src/vcfa_policy/client.py` is a stub. Implement its three methods.

`get_policy_type(type_id)` -- call the contract's `getPolicyType` operation and return the decoded `PolicyType`. Raise `PolicyTypeNotFoundError` (from `vcfa_policy.errors`) on 404, and `ApiError` on any other non-2xx.

`get_policy(policy_id)` -- call `getPolicy` and return the decoded `Policy`, or `None` on 404. Raise `ApiError` on any other non-2xx.

`ensure_policy(...)` -- converge a single policy, then return the policy as stored on the appliance:

1. Validate `type_id` through `get_policy_type` first. If the policy type does not exist, nothing may be mutated.
2. Send the contract's `createOrUpdatePolicy` mutation carrying `policy_id`, `type_id`, `name` and `definition`. `description`, `enforcement_type`, `project_id` and `org_id` are optional: pass them through when the caller supplies them, and keep them off the wire entirely when the caller does not. `null`, `""` and `{}` are all wrong -- the appliance treats "absent" and "explicitly cleared" as different requests.
3. The documented success responses carry no body, so read the stored policy back and return that.

This runs in CI behind a flaky load balancer, so it has to survive a lost response. Because `createOrUpdatePolicy` returns nothing on success, a 503 leaves the caller unable to tell whether the write landed. Retry the statuses the contract marks retryable, up to `max_attempts`, sleeping `backoff(attempt)` between attempts, and make sure the retry converges on the same policy instead of leaving a second one behind. Statuses the contract marks non-retryable must surface as `ApiError` immediately, without a second attempt. When the attempts run out, raise the last error.

Constraints:

- Python 3.9+ standard library only. No third-party packages. The only host the client may contact is the `base_url` it was constructed with.
- Do not edit `tests/`, `docs/contract.json` or `docs/official_sources.json`.
- `bash run_verification.sh` must pass.
reference_patch_apply: git apply -p1 --directory=files reference_fix.patch (from the seed root)
deliverable: src/vcfa_policy/client.py implementing PolicyClient.get_policy_type, get_policy and ensure_policy.

verification.notes: Runs tests/test_contract.py against the loopback mock in tests/vcfa_mock.py. The mock binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, builds its routing table from docs/contract.json so it serves only the three operations the contract names, and appends every request it receives to a JSONL log the tests read back. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. The mock has no clock and no randomness: timestamps and any server-minted ids are counter-derived.

contract_provenance.note: VCF Automation is absent from the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository and ships no OpenAPI document on the Broadcom Developer Portal. docs/contract.json was transcribed by hand on 2026-08-11 from the developer.broadcom.com xAPIs reference pages, and says so in its own source_statement. docs/official_sources.json records each page URL, the operation it documents and the fetch date.
